purpose: Convert a desired amp-envelope attack time to an E4XT rate byte WITHOUT fitting an exponential. The SHAPE comes from the machine's own table; only the SCALE is fitted.
model: t90(byte) = C / T[byte]      -- NO offset term
fitted_on: bytes 25 and 100 only; the other rungs are held out
table_source: EOS 4.70 decompressed OS, body offset 0x41490, 128 entries u16 big-endian. BYTE-IDENTICAL to EOS 4.62 (RESOLUTION_NOTES 126), so this is not version-fragile.
table_identified_by: RESOLUTION_NOTES 127 -- the envelope segment stepper at body 0x3fb38 indexes it as table[(field+modulation)>>5 clamped 0..127] and multiplies by elapsed ticks. Identified by its consumer, not by curve shape.
measurement_conditions: P017 of the flat-noise calibration bank: sample 11, origkey 72, note 72 root-matched so nothing is resampled; amp envelope a rectangle apart from Atk1; Q 0; no modulation cords. t90 = first crossing of 0.9 x plateau, 2 ms RMS smoothing. Each rung measured twice (spreads 0.020/0.000/0.000/0.080 s at 20 ms).
WHY_THE_TABLE_WINS: Not by much in the middle -- all four rungs sit where any exponential does well. The table's advantage is at the ENDS, where it is a factor of 2-3 rather than a few percent: the table's log-slope is 0.128 below byte 20 against a fitted 0.0565, so RESOLUTION_NOTES 122 measured firmware/single-exponential at 0.499 at byte 12 and 0.302 at byte 5. A lookup has no error there because it IS the machine's data.
CAVEATS: C and t0 are a TIME calibration tied to this project's t90 convention (0.9 of plateau, 2 ms smoothing) and to one preset at one note. They are not properties of the machine. Change the detector and they must be re-fitted. The TABLE is the machine's; the two constants are ours.
t0 = 17 ms is most likely the detector's own floor rather than device behaviour -- RESOLUTION_NOTES 130's no-attack control reports 20-60 ms with no rise present.
byte 55 measures 4% ABOVE every model including the table's own prediction. Either a real wrinkle in that region or a systematic at that rung; four points cannot tell.
The law is genuinely piecewise (RESOLUTION_NOTES 134, measured table-free): bytes 60-100 give k~0.0564 and bytes 25-55 give k~0.0587. A single constant is wrong in one band whichever value is chosen.
t0_seconds_REMOVED: mpc2emu's correction, adopted: t0 = 17.4 ms is the DETECTOR's floor (130's no-attack control reports 20-60 ms with no rise present), so it belongs to the measurement and not to the law. Subtract it from measured times when calibrating C; do not carry it into a converter. With t = C/T[byte] and nothing else, this project's detector convention survives in exactly ONE multiplicative constant -- every RATIO is the machine's own, so a later re-measurement with a better detector moves one number and cannot change the shape.
ACCURACY_CLAIM_CORRECTED: An earlier exchange reported the table reproducing the measured 25->100 ratio to four decimal places. THAT IS CIRCULAR: C and t0 were solved from bytes 25 and 100, so subtracting t0 and taking the ratio of those same two points recovers T[25]/T[100] exactly whatever the table contains. The HELD-OUT rungs are the test, and they are weaker: byte 60 misses by +0.83%, byte 55 by -3.91%, and the 55->60 ratio by +4.93%. So these data confirm the table's shape to about 4-5%, not to four decimals, and nearly all of the residual is the byte-55 wrinkle.
WHAT_JUSTIFIES_THE_TABLE: NOT these four rungs -- they all sit mid-range where any exponential does well, and they confirm the shape only to 4-5%. The justification is that the table IS the machine's own data, identified by its consumer (127), and that a single exponential is wrong by a FACTOR OF 2-3 at the ends (firmware/ours = 0.499 at byte 12, 0.302 at byte 5, per 122). Nothing measured on 2026-09-14 samples that region. The argument is 'this is the machine's table', not 'it fits our measurements better'.
